title: Diamond and graphite: one element, two structures
examples: Why is diamond hard but graphite soft?

explain.say: A sparkling diamond ring and the grey tip of your pencil are made of exactly the same atoms: carbon! How can that be? Look at the board. You can see the two side by side.

draw.text: Diamond and graphite: one element, two structures

explain.say: See diamond on the left? Every carbon atom is joined to four others by strong covalent bonds, in a giant 3D network. Nothing can slide. That makes diamond the hardest natural material. Why do you think drill tips are coated with diamond?

To cut through rock! Now look at graphite on the right. Each carbon joins only three others, in flat sheets of hexagons, like chicken wire. The sheets are only weakly held together, so they slide. What happens when you press your pencil on paper?

Layers rub off as your line! Look at the reasons on the board. In graphite, each carbon uses only three electrons in bonds, so one is free to move, and moving electrons carry electricity. Diamond uses all four. Which one do you think is used in batteries?

draw.question: Why does graphite conduct but diamond does not?

because.label: Three bonds each
because.note: Each carbon uses 3 of 4 outer electrons.

draw.answer: Graphite has free electrons; diamond uses all four in bonds

explain.say: Graphite! Great work. Both need over 3,500 °C to melt, because so many strong bonds must break. Wow: a single layer of graphite is called graphene. It is one atom thick, yet stronger than steel for its weight. Imagine what you could build with it!

faq.a: Each carbon atom is held by four strong covalent bonds in a rigid 3D network. To scratch diamond you must break many of these bonds.
asks: What makes diamond the hardest substance?

faq.q: Why is graphite soft and slippery?
faq.a: Graphite is made of flat layers of carbon atoms. The forces between the layers are weak, so the layers slide over each other easily.
asks: Why is graphite used in pencils?

faq.a: Each carbon in graphite bonds to only three others, so one outer electron per atom is free to move along the layers and carry a current.
Allotropes are different forms of the same element, with the atoms arranged differently. Diamond, graphite, graphene and fullerenes are allotropes of carbon.
Graphene is a single layer of graphite, just one atom thick. It is very strong, light and an excellent conductor.

facts: In diamond each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds; in graphite each forms three, leaving one delocalised electron per atom.
Graphene, a single layer of graphite, was first isolated in 2004 at the University of Manchester.
